builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PRISM: Causal Counterfactual Minimization of Agent Tool Privileges via Information Bottleneck Role Induction
summary: Replaces coarse, manually assigned or full-permission tool grants over MCP with automatically induced least-privilege roles derived from sandboxed counterfactual interventions and information-bottleneck compression. Costs include an offline phase of sandboxed trajectory collection, intervention experiments, and bilevel optimization with a generative flow network, plus ongoing role re-derivation when tools or tasks change; the inference overhead at runtime is small, but the pipeline adds significant engineering complexity. It can fail when sandbox interventions do not cover real task variability, causing necessary tools to be pruned and degrading task success, or when the rate-distortion knee selects too few roles and forces over-broad grants within a role.
rationale: Least-privilege tool scoping is directly applicable to API-based agent deployments on a limited budget, but the reported gains are benchmark-specific and the multi-stage pipeline requires workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: Counterfactual tool-privilege minimization for MCP agents

claims.statement: Replaces coarse, manually assigned or full-permission tool grants over MCP with automatically induced least-privilege roles derived from sandboxed counterfactual interventions and information-bottleneck compression. Costs include an offline phase of sandboxed trajectory collection, intervention experiments, and bilevel optimization with a generative flow network, plus ongoing role re-derivation when tools or tasks change; the inference overhead at runtime is small, but the pipeline adds significant engineering complexity. It can fail when sandbox interventions do not cover real task variability, causing necessary tools to be pruned and degrading task success, or when the rate-distortion knee selects too few roles and forces over-broad grants within a role.

Compresses authorized tools per role by 78.3% (to 21.7% of the original set), with 78.2% task success, 88.7% counterfactual necessity accuracy, and blast radius reduced to 15.9% on AgentDojo, tau-bench, and ToolEmu.
